title: #nexttonormal #westend #broadway #musicaltheatre #foryou
transcript: the West End revival of next to normal is a little bit overhyped in my opinion but to be clear I'm not confused by the hype that it's getting in the UK where it's never played before because I do think it's a really strong production of what I still think is a remarkably good musical so like why shouldn't it get hyped there? but I am a bit confused by all the hype I've heard from American people who have gone to see it who also saw the original. it's not even necessarily that I thought the original was better I think it was probably about on par in which case I was kind of just like “yeah, like that was…that was next to normal, it was very good!” I did enough research beforehand to know that it wasn't gonna be some massive reinvention of the material but I did think there would be maybe just a bit more to set it apart I think what was most overhyped for me was the casting I did love Caissie Levy's performance I thought she was easily the best in the cast I do think Jack Wolfe was very good probably the best casting I've seen in that role I wouldn't say it was like the next-level brilliant performance that I had been led to expect and you know normally I really like Jamie Parker but sadly his take on the role just didn't really come together for me now having said all that to be clear: I was still a puddle on the floor by the end I mean I was just sobbing probably even harder than I did when I saw the original because I think maybe I have the added layer of nostalgia plus just 14 more years of life experience So when I say it's overhyped I really don't mean that as a criticism of what the director actually did with it I thought he did justice to the material it was really focused and well paced but all the buzz around this production may be transferring to New York I don't know I mean I think it's been long enough that a New York revival wouldn't be inappropriate but I don't see any particular need for it to be this specific production other than that it's just like…right there finally though I do wanna talk about the one directorial decision I noticed that I do think significantly reframed something in the text over the years there has been some reasonable criticism against the show for how they chose to end Diana's story and also just for maybe a little bit demonizing psychiatric medicine but this production has a very small but effective directorial choice right at the end that for me alleviated that significantly. I'm not sure how confident I feel in the next thing I'm gonna say I'm kind of just thinking out loud and I would be curious to hear other people's thoughts but I can't help but wonder if the increase in conversation around the topic of mental health that we've had since this musical premiered has kind of, in a weird roundabout way, helped the show age even better psychiatric medicine *is* complicated and it *is* imperfect and experiences do vary so much from person to person and so as we diversify representation in media on this topic I wonder if there's less of an inclination to feel like next to normal is like “this is what people with mental illness experience” and instead just be like “this is *an* experience with mental illness.”
